newsitem.title: INDIA: Kalashnikov says AK-47's misuse makes him sad.
newsitem.headline: Kalashnikov says AK-47's misuse makes him sad.

text.p: Mikhail Kalashnikov says his assault rifle's reputation as a terrorist's weapon of choice can make him glum.
"It is a means of securing peace," the Russian said of his brainchild, the AK-47. "I feel very sad when I hear of its misuse."

Kalashnikov, 78, who spoke to the Press Trust of India while on a visit to a defence exhibition, said he designed the rifle to protect his fatherland, not to be used in hijackings and gangster shootouts.

"In no way am I responsible for its misuse by terrorists and other rebel groups across the world," said Kalashnikov, adding that he would like to be remembered for "my contribution towards saving my country's sovereignty and integrity".
In February, Russia celebrated the AK-47's half century with an exhibition in Moscow showing dozens of the hundred-odd versions of Kalashnikov's basic 1947 design.
The much-decorated Kalashnikov, who was a humble sergeant when he designed the AK-47, said now he makes hunting guns.
"It is for sports," he said. "I would like to be known for my constructive designs.
"I was born in a farmer's family," he added. "Had there been no World War, I would have designed some agricultural tool for the benefit of humanity."
